terms.scope: Use Bao-yu for Jia Bao-yu when the context identifies him. Keep the reported Zhen boy and the dream counterpart distinct; a shared name does not establish shared knowledge.
Use Dai-yu for Lin Dai-yu. Her advice, distress and jokes belong to the present scene; do not import a settled marriage or later fate.
Use Bao-chai for Xue Bao-chai, distinct from Bao-qin. Keep her advice, teasing and private generosity tied to their audiences.
Use Bao-qin for Xue Bao-qin, distinct from Bao-chai. Her engagement to the Mei family does not settle another character’s marriage.
Use Xiang-yun for Shi Xiang-yun. Her teasing and sympathy vary with the scene; figurative descriptions are not medical judgements.
Use Xi-feng in narration for Wang Xi-feng. Choose Mrs Lian and other direct addresses according to speaker and relationship; do not confuse her with Felicity.
Use Grandmother Jia for the household elder. Distinguish reported opinions, orders and jokes from completed decisions.
Use Lady Wang for Bao-yu’s mother, not for every occurrence of a general title such as madam or Her Ladyship.
Use Lady Xing for Jia She’s wife, distinct from her niece Xing Xiu-yan.
Use Aroma for Xi-ren. Respectful or teasing titles do not establish a new marriage or status.
Use Skybright for Qing-wen. Keep her shifting responses, sharp speech and violence rather than making sympathy erase them.
Use Musk for She-yue, distinct from Aroma. Her authority and observations belong to her own speeches.
Use Patience for Ping-er. Her tact, protection and authority operate within the household hierarchy.
Use Faithful for Yuan-yang, distinct from Oriole and the maid Parrot. Ordinary mandarin ducks are not this person.
Use Caltrop for Xiang-ling. Do not introduce a new transliterated everyday name.
Use Oriole for Bao-chai’s maid Ying-er, distinct from Faithful and the dramatic heroine Ying-ying.
Use Nightingale for Dai-yu’s maid Zi-juan, distinct from Snowgoose; ordinary birds do not take her name.
Use Zhui-er for the dismissed maid, distinct from Zhuan-er. The name does not apply to pendants or other objects.
Use Pin-pin for the affectionate form referring to Dai-yu; Little Pin-pin is possible where the tone warrants it. Do not replace her narrative name everywhere.
Use House of Green Delights for Bao-yu’s residence, with established contextual shortening where appropriate. A poetic image is not automatically the place.
Use Doctor Wang for the physician so named. The surname alone does not establish his full personal name.

Use Parfumée, including the accent, for the actress assigned to Bao-yu. This continues the project’s own chapter 81 name and the current chapter 54 choice. Preserve historical forms as history; do not import her later departure.
Only the maid, including Oriole’s familiar 小燕. In the chapter 59 title, retain the bird-name play without substituting an ordinary swallow for the person.
Swallow’s mother and Parfumée’s godmother, verified against author paragraph 81.24. The earlier unnamed godmother can remain unnamed until the narrative supplies the surname.
Ou-guan’s godmother, Swallow’s maternal aunt and Chan-jie’s maternal grandmother. Do not confuse her with the unnamed paternal aunt who guards flowers.
Mamma He’s younger daughter, not another name for Swallow. Do not invent a translated bird name solely from the character 鸠.
The girl trained in young male roles. She loves Di-guan and subsequently cares for Rui-guan. Preserve the relationship without identifying her sex by her stage role.
The girl in young female roles, assigned to Bao-chai. Her gift to Parfumée is not the packet later substituted for Jia Huan.
The deceased girl who played opposite Ou-guan. Her identity is disclosed in Parfumée’s private account at 58.37, not at the first sight of burning paper.
The girl trained in older male roles and assigned to Tan-chun. Her account in 60.26 distinguishes observation from inference.
The girl in comic painted-face roles, assigned to Bao-qin. Keep her position in the four-girl struggle distinct.
The girl trained in older female roles, requested by You-shi. This is a provisional project transliteration, not a botanical identification.
Mamma Xia’s granddaughter, serving in Tan-chun’s quarters. Do not translate 老娘 in her warning as her mother.
Liu’s daughter, sixteen and fifth among the siblings. Use the surname at identification and Wu-er thereafter; she has not yet been appointed.
The woman managing the garden kitchen and mother of Wu-er. Mrs Liu is an appropriate direct address, not a personal given name. Her brother and his son are separate from Qian Huai.
Aunt Zhao’s nephew and Jia Huan’s attendant. His threatened pressure to obtain Wu-er is not consent to a marriage.
The bamboo steward named at chapter 56 block 17 and seen at chapter 57 block 4. Do not identify an unrelated woman from a matching surname.
The woman with farming experience selected for the rice and vegetable plot.
Tealeaf’s mother and Oriole’s godmother; the proposed fragrant-plant stewardship follows that relationship.
A visitor named with Lin Zhi-xiao’s wife during Bao-yu’s illness. Do not erase the second woman or make her a male visitor.
Xiu-yan’s father. His and his wife’s assent is distinct from Lady Xing’s agreement.
Dai-yu’s maid, as in the complete author paragraphs 82.14 and 82.32. Do not merge her with Nightingale.
The maid assigned temporarily to Dai-yu during Nightingale’s vigil, and later one of Grandmother Jia’s attendants. The material amber in an object is not this person.
Grandmother Jia’s maid, confirmed in author paragraph 83.10. A colour, stone or bird elsewhere does not acquire this name.
Only the named maid among Grandmother Jia’s attendants at 59.2. Bottle glass elsewhere remains an ordinary material.
Lady Wang’s maid, who remains behind in chapter 59. Do not treat every silver object as a person.
Tan-chun’s maid, verified against complete author paragraphs 85.86–87 and the accepted chapter 37 letter scene.
The maid who recognizes the substituted jasmine powder. She is not silently merged with Cai-xia.
Lady Wang’s other named maid in the departure preparations. Preserve the distinction from Cai-yun.
The same servant under the two source names. His mother’s assignment does not assign the task to him.

The same maid now called Crimson, whose former place is mentioned at 60.39 under her original Chinese name 红玉. Preserve the current identity form rather than reviving a historical Hong-yu instruction; this is not a global replacement of the words red and jade.
Bao-yu’s nurse. Her panic and care are not medical authority.
The older nurse helping in the vigil. Do not conflate her with Mamma He or infer that every 宋妈 in every chapter has the same function.
A woman distinct from her husband. The surname Lin triggers Bao-yu’s fear, but she is not a member of Dai-yu’s household.
The steward, including the garden comparison and external household supervision. Keep Lai Sheng distinct.
Aunt Xue considers and then rejects him as Xiu-yan’s match. Later teasing does not settle a marriage to Dai-yu.
Distinguish the reported real boy from the dream counterpart and from Jia Bao-yu. Do not add his surname to every dream occurrence if the original preserves uncertainty.
The former theatrical training quarters. Do not create a separate Pear Fragrance Court.
Dai-yu’s residence. The poetic name Naiad is not itself a second building.
Bao-chai’s residence. The name does not certify modern plant species growing there.
Li Wan’s garden residence and the associated plots. Do not replace the existing name merely to regularize rice terminology.
The named bridge. Keep the associated pavilion and stream separate.
The complete name in chapter 59, not a substring replacement from the earlier 叶渚 entry. Its willow imagery must remain visible.

Chapter 59’s title writes 绛云轩, while the established room name is 绛芸轩. The same place uses the existing English name. Preserve the Chinese variant and record the identity decision rather than correcting it.
The capital in the imagined household’s speech. Do not harmonize every geographical expression into modern Beijing.
Dai-yu’s reported home and the destination in Nightingale’s invented departure story.
The named burial location in this fictional narrative. Do not assign a verified modern geographical location.
The Xue-funded shop on West Drum Tower Street. Preserve the embarrassing joke about the clothes arriving before their owner.
A directional street name, not a claim that the shop is a verified surviving business.
The deceased senior imperial woman. Do not call her the Dowager Princess of Beijing or of Nan’an.

The senior dowager in the Prince of Beijing’s household. Distinguish her from the younger princely consort and from the deceased imperial consort. The title-family comparator in author chapter 85 does not identify this woman.
The younger princely consort in the Prince of Beijing’s household. The author’s chapter 85 Nan’an title is a structural comparator, not evidence that these women are the same person.
Women entitled to rank and ritual attendance. Do not turn every female family member into an official or imply that ordinary subjects have the same obligations.
Parfumée’s role type, not her sex or a modern leading-lady employment contract.
Rui-guan’s role type; preserve prior project explanation rather than importing an external translated stage taxonomy.
Ou-guan’s role type, performed by a girl.
Kui-guan’s role category. Do not convert a face-paint category into an assertion of the performer’s physical appearance.
Dou-guan’s role category, distinct from Kui-guan’s.
Ai-guan’s theatrical category. It does not mean a foreigner.
Qie-guan’s theatrical category, not her actual age.
The actresses’ older female sponsors and the named household relationship. This does not imply Christian baptism or legal adoption. Own 81.12 uses godmothers for these women.
The status insult at 60.17 follows accepted 36.14. It is not a number and is not permission to change the source to 奴才.
Only Nightingale’s case holding the small mirror at 57.32. Chinese dictionary evidence supports the women’s toilet-case sense, not stationery.

Reuse the flower-patterned mirror root from accepted 28.49 and add the source’s small size. Ministry of Education entries explain 菱花 as a mirror name associated with a floral pattern on the back. Do not assert a particular outline, number of points or metal composition.
The fragrant medicinal powder used for an itch and valued as Rui-guan’s gift. The Chinese dictionary verifies the category, not its exact chemical composition, rose species or modern efficacy.
The cosmetic substitute. Do not call it the same substance as rose medicinal powder or add a diagnosis from the substitution.

Reuse the established Rose Essence root from accepted 34.17 and B07-ER1-113, with ordinary lower case in narration. Chapter 60 has a different stated bottle size and red liquid; this does not prove it is the same physical bottle. Preserve the title’s raw 玖 and selected 玫 separately. Do not introduce rose cordial, add alcohol or specify formulation, concentration or efficacy.

Retain the established fuling root from the project’s earlier medicine scene. Frost describes the named white preparation; neither this term nor the characters’ claims certify species, recipe, purity or benefit.
The medicine name already present in accepted chapter 28. Its occurrence inside fuling frost does not justify replacing it with a new English biological name.
The conveyance in chapter 59. Chinese transport evidence supports carriage by pack animals. The novel does not supply the precise animal count or construction described in later local histories.
The domestic interior at 56.1. The dictionary’s chapter-specific example supports this sense. Do not change 壸 to 壶 or render it as a pot.

Ou-guan’s manner of departure after entrusting her secret to Bao-yu at 58.21, not the older woman’s departure. The dictionary relates 佯常 to 佯长; preserve the contextual manner without correcting the Chinese spelling.
The godmother’s accusation in the hair-washing quarrel. Dictionary evidence for 掰 in the sense of talking nonsense supports the accusation, not its truth.
Xiang-yun’s complaint at 59.6. Keep the historical symptom description without declaring ringworm, an allergy or a modern diagnosis.
A document exchanged and concealed. It is not a debt ledger page; that is Xiang-yun’s mistaken first question.
Keep strings separate from taels of silver. Do not assign a universal modern monetary value or silently convert strings to a fixed number of coins.

Use catty after one or half a, and catties for plural quantified mass. At chapter 60 block 30, the two catties of cake are promised, not delivered. Preserve quantities and avoid modern weight conversion; names and idioms require their own senses.
Chapter 56’s gift list has no scarlet modifier, so reuse the figured-satin root without importing scarlet from an earlier compound.
Preserve the motif and material. The first gift group lists figured and python-pattern satin together with twelve bolts, not twelve of each.
The gift-list textile designation does not itself establish who manufactured it or its exact weave.
The source’s designation in the gift list; do not add embroidery or conflate it with B11’s separately scoped embroidered gauze.
The cloth wrapping Dai-yu’s eating utensils. Western describes the source designation, not a verified country of manufacture.
Compare own 81.48–50 for the mechanical boat on display. Keep the fear-driven hiding in chapter 57 distinct from the later gift and its later owner.
At chapter 58 block 10, retain early breakfast and breakfast as meals, distinct from the explicitly named noon and evening sacrifices.
The author’s choice at 58.14 is retained. Do not substitute the older common-edition reading merely because it is more familiar.
Use Temple of the Iron Threshold for the Qingming destination at chapter 58 block 13. Jia Lian’s party and Jia Rong’s party remain distinct.
The Warring States figure in Xiang-yun’s name comparison. He is distinct from the Han writer Sima Xiang-ru.
The Han figure sharing the given name Xiang-ru. Do not make the example assert physical likeness.
Only the thinker in the comparison and learned discussion; not the current narrator’s endorsement of a doctrinal claim.
The person for whom Confucius was mistaken in the cited story. Their names are different.
The thinker referred to by Bao-chai and Tan-chun. The named essay’s attribution remains the novel’s, without a claim of separately authenticated authorship.
Retain both named thinkers in the teasing about profit and learning.
The two sage rulers in the partial quotation. Only the supplied quoted passage is translated.
Retain the Jizi attribution as it appears in the novel without identifying an unverified author or completing the withheld next line.
The disciple invoked through the legend of understanding birds, not a character present in the garden.
Two separate figures named in Dai-yu’s mock-heroic comparison at 57.64. Retain both and do not turn Xiang-yun’s protest into an actual assassination plan.

terms.form: the Old Man under the Moon
terms.scope: The matchmaker in Aunt Xue’s red-thread explanation. This is a story told by a character, not a newly verified supernatural fact.
The heroine used in Musk’s comparison of Parfumée’s appearance. She is not Oriole and not a newly performed stage character in the room.
The maid from the dramatic comparison. Preserve her distinction from Ying-ying and do not quote unprovided lyrics.
Only an explicitly quantified physical length, such as the bottle’s approximately five cun at 60.36. The expression 尺寸地方儿 at 58.18 is not a measured floor area.

excludedSourceHits.reason: 尺寸地方儿 means a place governed by rules here, not a quantified area. The editorial scope already excludes it; the raw substring hit is not a cun application.

terms.form: the middle of the wei hour
terms.scope: The threshold after which the mourners return at 58.2. Preserve the traditional time division without adding an exact modern clock time.
The window gauze named in the chapter 58 title. Madder-red denotes the colour in this choice, not a verified dye recipe or fibre identification.
Dai-yu sends Snowgoose to inquire about Bao-yu at chapter 57 block 26. No catch or fastening is present.
The common household staff sent to buy the girls’ supplies at chapter 56 block 4, contrasted with individually chosen relatives or nurses. This denotes people, not money.

termExclusions: 宝玉 can identify a person, a dream counterpart or the jade object. Qualify Jia and Zhen only when the narrative situation warrants it; a substring match does not decide identity.
玻璃 at 59.2 names the maid Glass, but the small bottle at 60.36 is made of glass. 琥珀, 翡翠 and 金 are likewise not automatic personal names.
姑娘 in Swallow’s account identifies her paternal aunt; elsewhere it can be a mistress, a maid’s respectful address or a girl. No global replacement is safe.
梅香 is a conventional maid name in the saying, not a newly introduced servant. 奴几 has the inherited servant-status meaning, not a numeral.
柳叶渚 is a full place name. The earlier 叶渚 entry does not establish a mechanical substring substitution; ordinary willow leaves remain leaves.
金线 in a willow image is not literal gold-thread embroidery. 纱 in the chapter 56 list does not acquire the chapter 53 embroidered modifier.

钱粮 in the garden proposal is income or supplies in context, not automatically a funeral allowance or formal imperial grain tax. 斤 in the cake promise is weight; 一斤斤 elsewhere would require lexical review.
满纸, 写字纸, 烧纸, 当票 and 请帖 are different paper objects. The protective claim about discarded writing paper is not the narrator’s identification of the paper burned for Di-guan.
贾环’s acceptance, Cai-yun’s recognition, Aunt Zhao’s grievance and Mamma Xia’s encouragement are different facts, not a single agreed account of an insult.
Later events in author chapters 81–85 support names, diction and explicit recollections only. They do not supply future appointments, deaths, departures, engagements or knowledge to chapters 56–60.
At 57.26, 消息 means news, not a catch or fastening.
The servant-origin rule excludes 家里的旧例 at 56.22, 外头的银硝 at 60.10 and 家里的钱 at 60.40. Only the release report at 60.3 supports that sense here.
At 56.4, 官中的人 denotes household staff; the funds sense is limited to the monetary contexts at 56.15 and 56.24.

voices.speaker: Tan-chun
voices.guidance: Her questions proceed through costs, authority and workable arrangements. She can be wounded, angry and restrained in the same scene. In the quarrel she gives Aunt Zhao a face-saving exit, then insists on rank and procedure. Do not convert this into modern egalitarian management or permanent emotional coldness.

voices.speaker: Bao-chai
voices.guidance: Learned teasing, practical restraint and privately generous action coexist. She distinguishes public appearance from private aid and actively controls who hears about the pawned coat. Her fiscal advice is not a secret engagement plan; her childish intimacy with Aunt Xue is real.

voices.speaker: Patience
voices.guidance: She protects Xi-feng’s position while allowing Tan-chun’s reforms to succeed. Tact and authority do not eliminate hierarchy. Her reported command in chapter 59 must not be narrated as punishment already administered.

voices.speaker: Li Wan and You-shi
voices.guidance: Keep Li Wan’s assent, practical participation and imperfect oversight distinct from You-shi’s reluctant mediation and competing obligations. Neither woman simply hands the household to Aunt Xue or disappears from management.

voices.speaker: Bao-yu
voices.guidance: His tender solicitude, social privilege, panic, subsequent pretence and inventive protection are different actions. The initial illness is not a calculated performance. His private religious theory belongs to him, and his kindness does not make him understand every financial or labour consequence.

voices.speaker: Nightingale and Snowgoose
voices.guidance: Nightingale moves from propriety and deliberate testing to urgent care and practical marital counsel. Snowgoose’s explanations and errands are not malicious disclosure. Their later author-chapter care provides continuity of diction, not knowledge of future illness.

voices.speaker: Dai-yu
voices.guidance: Preserve the bodily force of distress, repartee, motherless grief and sympathy for Xiu-yan. Do not make every remark jealousy or turn all smiles into a mask. Her knowledge of the pawn ticket begins only with Bao-chai’s private explanation.

voices.speaker: Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang and Aunt Xue
voices.guidance: Grandmother Jia’s alarm interrupts the physician’s formula and turns to matchmaking humour later. Lady Wang speaks through family authority and concern. Aunt Xue can soothe, tease and act practically; her proposed Bao-yu and Dai-yu match is not an announcement of a settled decision.

voices.speaker: Doctor Wang and the nurses
voices.guidance: The physician’s diagnostic quotation, deferential answers and concern about fees have separate rhythms. Nurse Li’s alarming reaction worsens the panic; Nurse Song’s later watch is practical care. Historical medical language is neither a modern diagnosis nor endorsed advice.

voices.speaker: Parfumée and the other actresses
voices.guidance: Parfumée’s pride, affection, anger, charm and cruel teasing coexist. Ou-guan’s grief and Rui-guan’s attachment are not generalized mischief. Ai-guan’s accusation contains an inference, and Kui-guan and Dou-guan have their own actions in the fight. Do not use one comic servant dialect for them all.

voices.speaker: Aroma, Musk and Skybright
voices.guidance: Aroma mediates and supplies practical care. Musk invokes household rules and can recommend a contemptuous substitution. Skybright is sharp, changes sides in the washing dispute, urges dismissal and only pretends to stop the later fight while arranging intervention. None is a uniformly kindly modern carer.

voices.speaker: Oriole and Swallow
voices.guidance: Oriole’s skill and playful refusal to surrender the willow branches become dangerous when her joke is believed. Swallow’s family account is frank, frightened and observant. Her description of future freedom is reported hope, not an accomplished change in status.

voices.speaker: Mamma He, Mamma Xia and the paternal aunt
voices.guidance: Keep three people and their economic interests distinct. Mamma He’s violence turns to fear of losing her livelihood. Mamma Xia’s grievance over Ou-guan informs her incitement. The paternal aunt both guards flowers and later offers Oriole more. Avoid making all older women interchangeable villains.

voices.speaker: Aunt Zhao, Jia Huan and Cai-yun
voices.guidance: Jia Huan accepts the lesser powder before his mother stirs the quarrel. Cai-yun recognizes it and tries to dissuade Aunt Zhao. Aunt Zhao uses rank, humiliation and abuse; those claims remain her own, without added slurs, caricatured dialect or narrator approval.

voices.speaker: Liu’s wife, Wu-er and Chan-jie
voices.guidance: The kitchen mother’s flattery and gifts seek a place for her daughter. Wu-er has her own ambitions, weakness and refusal of an unwanted match. Chan-jie resents favouritism and responds sharply. Requests, gifts, promises and actual appointment must remain separate.

scenes.title: Duplicate allowances
scenes.readingAndExecution: Tan-chun distinguishes the girls’ two-tael monthly allowance from a separate two-tael cosmetics allocation. Patience explains purchasing and poor-quality goods. Li Wan’s agreement and the remembered school allowance belong to the same practical conversation, not a new annual calculation.

scenes.title: Garden income and literary banter
scenes.readingAndExecution: Tan-chun estimates garden income from the Lai household example. Bao-chai answers with learned teasing, then approves practical stewardship. Patience explains Xi-feng’s constraints, without making every objection the narrator’s verdict. The half-size comparison and four-hundred-tael estimate remain the speakers’ arithmetic.

scenes.title: Choosing garden stewards
scenes.readingAndExecution: Distinguish the women’s competing bids from the assignments selected. Mamma Zhu’s bamboo, Mamma Tian’s crops and Mamma Ye’s fragrant plants are specific tasks. Oriole’s mother has expertise but is not simply awarded the work; Bao-chai resists the appearance of favouring her own servants. Oriole has already called Mamma Ye her godmother.

scenes.title: Sharing benefits without new account-office control
scenes.readingAndExecution: Tan-chun proposes accounts; Bao-chai instead makes contractors supply specified household needs, retain a surplus and contribute strings of cash for the other garden women. The women welcome removal from the accounts office’s control. Promised vigilance is not proof of lasting harmony.

scenes.title: The Zhen household’s visit
scenes.readingAndExecution: Keep five gift groups and their separate quantities. Four women report on the other Bao-yu, aged thirteen, who has stayed with his grandmother. The Jia child’s courtesy contrasts with their report, but no meeting of the two boys occurs. Lady Wang’s belated arrival and servants’ comparisons retain their social setting.

scenes.title: Names, likeness and a nested dream
scenes.readingAndExecution: Xiang-yun distinguishes identical names from identical people through historical examples. Jia Bao-yu dreams of another household and another Bao-yu describing a reciprocal dream. Aroma wakes him; Musk’s mirror explanation is a belief she voices. The final summons continues into chapter 57, without an invented closing couplet.

scenes.title: Confirmation, propriety and an unintended hurt
scenes.readingAndExecution: The visit confirms that Zhen Bao-yu exists, not that the boys have met. Nightingale withdraws from touch on grounds of propriety. Snowgoose explains her borrowed-coat excuse and Aunt Zhao’s brother’s wake. Do not turn keeping vigil into an explicitly performed sacrifice or repair the chronology.

scenes.title: Nightingale’s test
scenes.readingAndExecution: Bao-yu explains his previously interrupted bird’s-nest proposal. Nightingale invents the return to Suzhou and the family’s preparations to test him. Her report to Skybright conceals that provocation. Neither claim becomes narrator-certified fact.

scenes.title: Collapse and competing responses
scenes.readingAndExecution: Bao-yu’s first collapse is involuntary. Nurse Li’s alarm, Aroma’s urgency, Dai-yu’s violent coughing and the elders’ reactions remain distinct. Lin Zhi-xiao’s wife’s name and a model boat trigger his fear. Doctor Wang’s historical phlegm explanation is interrupted by Grandmother Jia; her threats and his relief over the fee carry the scene’s comedy.

scenes.title: Recovery, attachment and private counsel
scenes.readingAndExecution: Once Bao-yu understands what happened, his continuing pretence is explicitly differentiated from his earlier illness. Nightingale explains her own family ties and Dai-yu’s dependence. Her counsel about securing a marriage while Grandmother Jia lives is advice, not an accomplished engagement or a prediction of a dated death.

scenes.title: A marriage is actually arranged
scenes.readingAndExecution: Aunt Xue rejects Xue Pan as a match for Xiu-yan and chooses Xue Ke. Xi-feng approaches Grandmother Jia, who secures Lady Xing’s agreement; Xiu-yan’s parents consent. You-shi and her daughter-in-law are the two intermediaries. Preserve joking self-deprecation, not literal disability. This engagement is real, unlike the subsequent Bao-yu and Dai-yu suggestion.

scenes.title: A pawned coat and discreet help
scenes.readingAndExecution: Xiu-yan explains losing half her allowance to her parents and paying Ying-chun’s servants. Bao-chai’s criticism gives way to practical help. The jade pendant is Tan-chun’s gift and is not to be discarded. Hengshu is a pawnshop funded by the Xue family; redemption is planned here, not narrated as already completed.

scenes.title: Motherly comfort and marriage teasing
scenes.readingAndExecution: Aunt Xue’s red-thread story remains her explanation of marriage. Dai-yu’s wish to call her Mother and Bao-chai’s jokes create intimacy, not formal adoption paperwork. The Xue Pan tease is disavowed. Aunt Xue then proposes Bao-yu and Dai-yu; no assent by their guardians is supplied.

scenes.title: The pawn ticket’s changing audience
scenes.readingAndExecution: Xiang-yun takes a ticket Oriole has put in a book. Bao-chai first supplies a cover story in front of Aunt Xue, then privately tells Dai-yu and Xiang-yun the truth. They stop when Tan-chun and Xi-chun arrive. Do not make the whole household know Xiu-yan’s hardship.

scenes.title: Imperial mourning and delegated care
scenes.readingAndExecution: The deceased elderly imperial consort is not a princess of Beijing. Keep titled-household and commoner prohibitions distinct, along with palace attendance and the later burial journey. You-shi’s childbirth is the reported excuse used to leave her behind. Aunt Xue cares for the girls and Dai-yu’s needs, without taking over household management.

scenes.title: Releasing and redistributing the actresses
scenes.readingAndExecution: The household proposes release, asks the girls and addresses the risk of resale. Twelve, four or five and the eight named assignments are left as stated. All these performers are girls; male and female stage roles do not change the performers’ sex. Freedom to leave and reassignment to domestic service are different outcomes.

scenes.title: Qingming, the apricot tree and Ou-guan
scenes.readingAndExecution: Keep early breakfast and the explicitly named noon and evening sacrifices separate. Bao-yu walks with a stick. 修树 means pruning the tree, following the author’s choice. His remembered poetic line connects fruit, children and Xiu-yan’s marriage in his own thoughts. Bird speech is his imagined understanding and a Gongye Chang allusion. The older women’s resentment follows the actresses’ reassignment. Jia Lian takes Jia Huan, Jia Cong and Jia Lan to the Temple of the Iron Threshold for Qingming offerings, while Jia Rong goes with other clan members. These are distinct parties.

scenes.title: Protective lies about burning paper
scenes.readingAndExecution: Ou-guan initially withholds whom she is mourning. Bao-yu first claims the paper was waste writing, then invents an apricot deity’s dream instruction. Do not merge the excuses or disclose Di-guan before Parfumée tells him. The older woman’s resentment does not prove her account of the girls.

scenes.title: Hair washing and household authority
scenes.readingAndExecution: Parfumée protests against her godmother’s unequal treatment. Skybright first blames the girl, then resists the older woman’s violence. Musk asserts household order, while Aroma provides supplies and mediation. Preserve insults and coercion without adding modern diagnoses or treating either side’s accusations as settled fact.

scenes.title: Clock, meal and the inner room
scenes.readingAndExecution: A broken clock pendulum and a watch are separate objects. Half a cup of tea’s time is not half an hour. Four small dishes, soup and the portion shared with Parfumée remain distinct. Her godmother’s attempt to blow on the soup breaches access to the inner room; Parfumée’s pretended headache enables the private conversation.

scenes.title: Stage marriage, real love and ritual sincerity
scenes.readingAndExecution: Parfumée reports Ou-guan’s love for the dead Di-guan and her kindness to Rui-guan afterward. Stage husband and wife and real attachment coexist. Do not reduce the relationship to ordinary friendship or impose modern identity labels. Bao-yu’s theory of sincere offerings is his requested message, not the narrator’s universal religious doctrine.

scenes.title: Departure and the guarded household
scenes.readingAndExecution: The returning elders later depart for the funeral. Six maids and ten older women exclude the men; the advance party is separate. Faithful and Silver remain at home. Grandmother Jia shares an animal-borne litter with Jia Rong’s wife, while Lady Wang has another. Most gates close, with two interior garden gates left open.

scenes.title: The powder errand and willow baskets
scenes.readingAndExecution: Oriole and Rui-guan go for Dai-yu’s rose medicinal powder for Xiang-yun’s itch. Oriole makes a first basket for Dai-yu and then starts another. Ou-guan carries Dai-yu’s utensils in a Western handkerchief. Willow threads described as gold are imagery, not metal.

scenes.title: Swallow explains the three older women
scenes.readingAndExecution: Mamma He is Swallow’s mother and Parfumée’s godmother. Mamma Xia is Swallow’s maternal aunt and Ou-guan’s godmother. The unnamed flower guardian is Swallow’s paternal aunt. Xiao-jiu is Swallow’s younger sister; 小女 does not establish that Swallow is the youngest. The profit from flowers helps explain strict guarding.

scenes.title: A teasing accusation becomes violence
scenes.readingAndExecution: Oriole jokingly blames Swallow for picking the flowers. Swallow’s paternal aunt takes it seriously, and her mother joins in. Preserve each blow, the chase, the fall and the basket’s disposal without making every action belong to the same old woman. Oriole’s quota argument is not a new general permission to pluck anything.

scenes.title: Threatened dismissal and a reprieve
scenes.readingAndExecution: Aroma and Musk protect Swallow, while Skybright urges dismissal. Patience’s forty-blow order is relayed, not carried out. Bao-yu allows Mamma He to stay after her promise. Patience arrives afterward. Her eight or nine troubles in three or four days remain approximate and mostly unreported.

scenes.title: Apology and a privately transferred gift
scenes.readingAndExecution: Bao-yu sends both Swallow and Mamma He to apologize to Oriole at Allspice Court and instructs them not to speak before Bao-chai, lest Oriole be reprimanded. At chapter 60 block 4, mother and daughter approach Oriole together, apologize, are offered tea and leave together. Rui-guan then asks them to carry her packet to Parfumée. Only after they return to Bao-yu’s rooms, at block 5, does Swallow enter alone while her mother stays out. Swallow and Bao-yu suppress a spoken report through their exchanged signals, and Swallow privately gives Parfumée the packet. Do not invent an independent act by Oriole of concealing the quarrel. Swallow’s report of future release remains a reported plan, not completed emancipation.

scenes.title: Substitution, recognition and incitement
scenes.readingAndExecution: Parfumée values Rui-guan’s gift, finds her own powder box empty, follows Musk’s advice and substitutes jasmine powder. Jia Huan accepts it despite Cai-yun recognizing the difference. Aunt Zhao turns the matter into a challenge to rank; Mamma Xia encourages her out of her own grievance. Neither change of motive is supplied by the narrator as justification.

scenes.title: The fight and Tan-chun’s intervention
scenes.readingAndExecution: Bao-yu is away. Aunt Zhao throws the powder and strikes Parfumée; the four other girls intervene with distinct positions. Skybright pretends to separate them but has sent Swallow for Tan-chun; Aroma genuinely tries to intervene. Tan-chun removes Aunt Zhao by a face-saving pretext, not by endorsing the assault.

scenes.title: An accusation that remains unproved
scenes.readingAndExecution: Tan-chun criticizes the loss of rank and orders an inquiry. Ai-guan reports whispering and her inference about Mamma Xia, while still accepting Bao-yu’s earlier cover story. Tan-chun does not certify the accusation. Ebony warns Chan-jie, Mamma Xia’s granddaughter; 老娘 here is the maternal grandmother.

scenes.title: Kitchen favours and a hoped-for place
scenes.readingAndExecution: Parfumée delivers Bao-yu’s request for cold sour vegetables without sesame oil. The cake provocation leads to a promise of two catties in recompense, not a completed payment. Liu’s daughter is sixteen, fifth in her family’s birth order, and frail. No appointment has yet been secured; the two vacancies are discussed later at block 39.

scenes.title: Rose essence and continuing promises
scenes.readingAndExecution: The narration briefly returns to Bao-yu’s response to the fight. He authorizes the remaining rose essence as a gift. The bottle, its red contents and the mistaken comparison with Western wine remain distinct. Parfumée renews her promise to seek a place for Liu Wu-er; the girl’s wishes and fear of coercive marriage remain her own.

scenes.title: Family sharing and fuling frost
scenes.readingAndExecution: Liu’s wife shares rose essence with her nephew. Qian Huai is Aunt Zhao’s nephew and Jia Huan’s attendant, not this sick nephew. Keep the small cup, dilution, remaining half and basket quantities without repairing them into a concentration calculation. The fuling frost comes through the uncle’s share of a gate gift; no theft is established. The gate summons leads into chapter 61.

materials.execution: Use household funds, monthly allowance and regular allowance in their established senses. Do not relabel the arrangements as leases or privatization. Crops, bamboo shoots, bird grain, fragrant herbs and flower sales remain different products. The rose types and baoxiang flowers need readable descriptive distinctions, not a modern taxonomic catalogue.

Keep roses, climbing roses, monthly-flowering roses, baoxiang flowers and honeysuckle in the source’s order. Baoxiang remains a plant name of uncertain modern identification. The Allspice Court name is not botanical proof, and profitable uses reported by Li Wan are not a verified trade manual.

The listed supplies replace household expenditure; surpluses support contractors and contributions support other garden women. Bao-chai weighs a further two or three hundred taels against household standing and speaks of four or five hundred taels saved outside. Preserve both estimates and their different roles.

Use figured satin and satin with python designs, followed by assorted satins, gauzes, palace silk and the mixed official-use satin, gauze, silk and damask group. Apply imperial-use and official-use modifiers to the stated groups. Do not add scarlet, embroidery or certified weave structures.

materials.topic: The large room mirror, portable mirrors and display boat
materials.execution: At chapter 56 block 48, Bao-yu sees his reflection in the large fitted room mirror, and Musk discusses the mirror cover and the bed placed near it. Keep that mirror separate from the two or three small mirrors in Nightingale’s dressing case at chapter 57 block 32, one of which Bao-yu asks to keep. The Western gold mechanical boat on the display shelves at chapter 57 block 22 is another object. Reuse flower-patterned mirror for the small 菱花 mirror without asserting a flower-shaped outline or identifying it with the earlier poetic mirror.

Padded clothes pawned for spending money and the lined clothes worn in the cold are different. Keep the jade pendant from Tan-chun and the pawn ticket separate. Redemption and delivery of the clothes are proposed, not already executed.

Rank governs attendance; family shrines and Buddhist nuns’ lodging coexist in the described arrangement. A godmother is a household and sponsorship relationship, not Christian baptism. Freeing an actress from performance and retaining her for domestic service are not the same as release from service.

Pruning, planting beans and setting lotus roots are separate work. Burning paper for the dead, discarded writing paper and an invented floral deity are separate accounts. Do not describe a real rite performed for the fictional apricot deity.

Oil, soap-like cleansing materials, towels, wash water and dried hair have practical functions in the dispute. Keep the clock’s faulty pendulum distinct from the watch. The ham-and-fresh-bamboo-shoot soup is not one of four small dishes. Blowing on hot soup is taught and then policed by rank.

The requested skin powder differs from ordinary cosmetic powder. Willow branches, leaves and picked flowers become baskets through Oriole’s handiwork. Gold-like young willow threads do not become embroidered gold wire. The first completed gift and the later discarded basket are distinct.

Track Rui-guan’s valued gift, Parfumée’s empty personal box, Musk’s suggestion, the substituted jasmine packet, Jia Huan’s retrieval and Cai-yun’s recognition. No exact chemical salt or medical diagnosis is established.

materials.topic: Kitchen food and two later gifts
materials.execution: Cold sour vegetables exclude sesame oil because Bao-yu dislikes their being greasy. Cakes are food used in teasing and waste; two catties is a restitution promise. Rose essence and fuling frost retain the existing project roots. The red drink is initially mistaken for Western grape wine, not confirmed to contain alcohol; the white preparation has no verified formula or modern therapeutic guarantee.

literary.execution: Retain the parallel praise of Tan-chun’s reform and Bao-chai’s broader judgement. Do not turn the title into a modern management slogan.

The text names Master Zhu’s piece on not abandoning oneself, then quotes a partial passage attributed to Jizi. Preserve the attribution as the novel gives it, without certifying the book’s author or inventing the sentence the speaker withholds. Only the selected working projection adds 窃. Confucius, Mencius, Yao and Shun remain distinguishable references.

Keep Bao-chai’s paired warning about the beginning and the end, and about polished words and appetite for gain. 幸于始 can suggest initial eagerness or satisfaction followed by slackness in this context; do not force it into accidental good fortune. This is cautious interpretive guidance, not a proved textual correction. Retain 幸 and 缮, and do not attach an unverified canonical source.

稳坐吃三注 invokes winning three stakes without effort. Preserve the gaming image in a readable phrase; it does not mean three official salaries. Public lexical evidence is contextual, not proof that a game is being played in the scene.
The gift list is an embedded quotation with five ordered groups. Its opening and close belong inside the surrounding household actions.

Lin Xiang-ru and Sima Xiang-ru share a name, while Confucius and Yang Hu furnish a likeness example. Keep the examples’ different logical roles. The dream contains another dream report and an interrupted recognition; do not flatten the quotation levels.
Read 莽玉 in the selected chapter title. Preserve Nightingale’s intelligent test and Aunt Xue’s affectionate comfort as parallel actions.

Doctor Wang quotes several causes of phlegm-clouded consciousness, then applies one to Bao-yu. Grandmother Jia cuts him short. Keep the medical book quotation separate from his diagnosis and from the narrator’s report.
The old-age proverb and the great-sum-for-a-confidant saying are spoken counsel. Keep their force without predicting a dated death or replacing money with a modern value.

The recollected core sentence in author 84.47 is: There, I've settled another matter. I wonder how much I'll get in matchmaker's fees. Reuse this exact core when translating the corresponding words, while also translating the source’s preceding 我爱管个闲事. Do not import the later card exchange, mourning or tears.
An invitation and a pawn ticket are mentioned, not fully transcribed documents. Translate the surrounding description and mistaken identification without inventing either document’s contents.
The old man under the moon, red thread and sea-spanning match are Aunt Xue’s explanation. Preserve playful embarrassment, the Xue Pan joke’s rejection and the separate Bao-yu and Dai-yu proposal.

The rabbit-and-fox proverb and Dai-yu’s Jing Ke and Nie Zheng comparison accompany sympathy and mock-heroic teasing. Do not make Xiang-yun announce an actual assassination or flatten the allusion into generic anger.

Male and female phoenix imagery connects stage husband and wife with genuine love. The girls are performers, not male bodies revealed under female names. Maintain the title’s fictive roles and real feeling without a modern label or a new explanatory plot. Preserve the madder-red gauze window in the other half of the title; the colour does not establish a dye recipe.
The imperial order is reported with specific prohibitions. Its formality is not permission to add a missing edict preamble or seal.

The quoted line 绿叶成荫子满枝 appears twice in Bao-yu’s thought. Use the same original English line twice, preserving leaves, shade, fruit and the association with children. Keep the novel’s 荫 spelling. The selected note explains the wordplay without adding an attribution or a prediction of pregnancy.

Gongye Chang’s understanding of birds belongs to legend and Bao-yu’s comparison. The bird’s supposed complaint is his imagined interpretation, not a narrator-certified translation from an animal language.

The protest that things cry out when wronged and the godmother’s lifelong authority claim belong to their respective speakers. Ying-ying and Hong-niang are dramatic comparisons, not a newly performed extract of The Western Chamber.

Ou-guan’s analogy with a widower remarrying reaches Bao-yu through Parfumée. Bao-yu then entrusts a reply about incense and sincere feeling. Preserve the two acts of reporting and all negations; do not turn the passage into an editorial essay on ritual.

Oriole and Swallow’s names carry the bird play; the second half turns domestic commands into a mock military dispatch. Use the established names and Crimson Rue Studio, while retaining the source’s 绛云 variant in provenance.

The girl, married woman and old woman maxim is Bao-yu’s opinion reported by Swallow. The author repeats its dead pearl and fish’s eye language at 81.24. Reuse those lexical images, without importing the later argument about which maid is leaving.
Keep all four substances distinct: jasmine powder, rose medicinal powder, rose essence and fuling frost. The title’s paired substitutions and consequences do not authorize spoiling later accusations.

梅香拜把子，都是奴几 uses a conventional maid name and sworn-sister image to deny a status difference. Preserve the insolence and the established servant sense. Mei-xiang is not a new character, and 几 is not a number.

Preserve the actual endings: a summons, a chapter-transition formula, a report of return, an unfinished conversation and a gate summons. There are no new closing poems to compose and no missing scene to supply.

quantitiesAndChronology.rule: Two taels per month for each girl and another two for cosmetics are distinct allowances. The school’s eight-tael allowance is an earlier annual comparison, not another monthly payment.
The Lai garden reportedly brings in two hundred taels despite being less than half the size. Tan-chun’s four-hundred-tael expectation stays her estimate; do not silently fix the arithmetic.
Retain the four enumerated benefits in their order. An annual silver return is a proposal at this stage, not a collected sum.

Bamboo shoots, grain for birds, plant supplies and unspecified strings of cash have different destinations. Contractors retain a surplus and contribute to the other women; there is no stated fixed rental rate.

Five gift groups have quantities twelve, twelve, twelve, twelve and twenty-four bolts. The first twelve cover figured satin and satin with python designs together. The total is seventy-two bolts, but do not replace the ordered list with that total.
Four visiting women are over forty. Zhen Bao-yu is reported as thirteen. Do not infer Jia Bao-yu’s age from their similarity.

One tael of bird’s nest each day is reported. Reuse the accepted chapter 45 weight terminology, distinguishing this tael of material from silver money. Bao-yu’s two or three years of use is his optimistic claim, not a medical guarantee.
The intervals of alarm, a night’s watch, gradual recovery and later pretence remain relative. Do not insert a modern diagnosis or a medically guaranteed recovery schedule.
Two or three mirrors is an approximate small count in the source. Bao-yu asks to keep one small mirror, not the entire dressing case.

Needlework gifts of two kinds and three or four days of birthday activity remain distinct. The source does not establish the total number of individual gift pieces. The booked short play is mentioned, but no performed text is supplied.
Two women act as intermediaries: You-shi and her daughter-in-law. The joking ten myriad taels is extravagant speech, not a fee paid or a dowry contract.

Xiu-yan’s two-tael monthly allowance loses one tael to her parents, while she also pays servants for food and drink every few days. Her pawn proceeds are several strings of cash. Bao-chai’s help and advice do not amend the formal allowance.
The Mei family is expected back the year after next; Xue Ke waits for his sister’s wedding before his own. Do not equate this with an exact modern calendar date or move the wedding earlier.
Bao-chai refers to seven or eight years earlier. Do not derive an exact age, year or new family chronology.

Titled households face one year without banquets and music; commoners face three months without marriage. Twenty-one days in the palace, about ten days for the return journey and roughly a month away are separate, approximate intervals.
Aunt Xue shares Dai-yu’s quarters because of the stated occupancy constraints. You-shi’s declared childbirth is an administrative excuse; do not calculate pregnancy or a newborn’s age.
Twelve actresses are considered; four or five wish to leave; eight are assigned by name. Each teacher receives eight taels. Preserve these numbers without forcing an exact reconciliation.

The fifth watch, snacks before entry, early breakfast, breakfast at the lodging, the noon and evening sacrifices and evening meal remain in the source’s order. Do not turn two explicit sacrifices into a third through mistranslation of 早膳.
Qingming and the apricot tree’s condition are textual markers. Do not harmonize this chronology with the chapter 57 wake or with another edition’s season.
Half a cup of tea’s time is a short interval, not thirty minutes. Four small dishes, the ham-and-bamboo-shoot soup and the bowls taken or shared must remain separate.
Six maids and ten older women follow, excluding men. Faithful and Silver stay home; the earlier departure of supplies is not counted as the same party. Two inner garden gates remain open.

Four or five hundred cash per month is the household surplus Swallow says followed her placement in the garden, alongside saving the expense of keeping her at home. It is not stated as profit from the flowers, and no extra three- or four-hundred-cash figure should be invented. The paternal aunt’s guarded plot is a separate source of hoped-for gain.
Forty blows are ordered through a messenger but not administered. Bao-yu’s reprieve and Patience’s later arrival remain distinct.
Eight or nine incidents in three or four days are Patience’s approximate account, not an exhaustive list the translation should invent.

Aunt Zhao strikes Parfumée twice. Ou-guan and Rui-guan hold her arms, while Kui-guan and Dou-guan press from front and back. Four helpers do not include Parfumée as a fifth attacker in those positions.
Parfumée promises to buy two catties of cake in recompense at chapter 60 block 30. This is a future promise, not a delivery or cash payment.
Wu-er is sixteen and fifth in her family’s birth order. Crimson’s and Zhui-er’s former places give two vacancies; a vacancy is not an appointment of Wu-er.

The small glass bottle is about five cun tall and contains less than half a bottle of red liquid. Reuse rose essence as a lexical root without changing the three-cun bottle in chapter 34 or asserting the same bottle.

Liu’s wife takes half a small cup for her nephew, who mixes and drinks a bowl; a remaining half-cup is covered. Preserve these narrative quantities without supplying an unmentioned dilution ratio or correcting the sequence.

Two small baskets of fuling frost go to the masters and a further basket goes to the gatekeepers. Wu-er’s uncle receives a share and her aunt offers some onward. Do not turn a share into a whole additional basket.

The suggested milk preparation and daily amount belong to the aunt’s account of use. Preserve the gift and the later summons without endorsing a modern prescription or revealing the next chapter’s investigation.

relationships.rule: Oriole’s mother has aromatic-plant expertise; Mamma Ye is Tealeaf’s mother. Oriole has already called Mamma Ye her godmother. Bao-chai’s proposal avoids a direct appearance of favouring her own household.
Bao-chai’s 姨娘 is Lady Wang, her aunt. This does not name Aunt Zhao or refer generically to a concubine.
Nightingale’s invented Lin relatives are part of her test. Her own parents and siblings are in the Jia household. Her attachment to Dai-yu does not erase those family ties.
Xue Ke is Bao-qin’s brother and Aunt Xue’s nephew; Xiu-yan is Lady Xing’s niece. Xue Pan is a different proposed match whom Aunt Xue rejects.

Bao-chai and Bao-qin have different relationships to Xue Ke. Do not translate both 大姑 and 小姑 as an unqualified pair of biological sisters. Aunt Xue’s Mother role toward Dai-yu is affectionate, not a completed legal adoption.

Assignments are Wen-guan to Grandmother Jia, Parfumée to Bao-yu, Rui-guan to Bao-chai, Ou-guan to Dai-yu, Kui-guan to Xiang-yun, Dou-guan to Bao-qin, Ai-guan to Tan-chun and Qie-guan to You-shi. These assignments do not import later author-chapter transfers.

The deceased imperial consort, the senior and younger consorts of the Prince of Beijing’s household are different people. The 许 named in the mourning list and Jia Rong’s wife in the travelling party must not silently be replaced with the deceased Qin-shi.
Ou-guan’s stage relationship with Di-guan and later Rui-guan is reported by Parfumée. The subsequent loving care does not prove she has forgotten Di-guan.

Mamma He is Swallow’s mother and Parfumée’s godmother. Mamma Xia is Swallow’s maternal aunt, Ou-guan’s godmother and Chan-jie’s maternal grandmother. The unnamed flower guardian is Swallow’s paternal aunt. Xiao-jiu is Swallow’s younger sister.
Liu’s wife and her brother are siblings; his son is Wu-er’s maternal cousin. Qian Huai is Aunt Zhao’s nephew and Jia Huan’s attendant. Do not merge the sick cousin with the unwanted suitor.

二爷, 奶奶, 姑娘, 姐姐, 妹妹, 姨娘 and 妈妈 require speaker and addressee identification. A respectful sister address does not establish biological kinship. A narrative name is not automatically the correct form of direct address.

anchor.text: He gazed up at the little apricots, unwilling to turn away. Then he remembered that a husband had been chosen for Xing Xiu-yan. Marriage was a great matter for men and women, certainly, and could not be dispensed with; yet it meant one lovely girl fewer. In no more than two years, for her too, ‘Green leaves have made a shade, and branches teem with fruit.’ A few more days and this tree’s fruit would fall, leaving its branches empty. A few more years and Xiu-yan’s raven hair would surely turn to silver, her rosy face wither. The thought grieved him. He stood there weeping and sighing over the apricot tree.

readerNotePolicy: Carry exactly the three selected texts after the complete specified segments. Do not expand their claims, reveal later events or treat a character’s belief as medical or historical certification.

sourceReadingLimits.guidance: Retain 内壸 as the domestic inner quarters. Do not replace 壸 with 壶 or translate it as a pot.
Project only the specified 窃 addition. Preserve the novel’s attribution without inventing an author or completing the next line deliberately withheld by the speaker.
Keep the speaker’s comparisons and four-hundred-tael estimate as stated. Do not revise the source to reconcile the arithmetic.
Retain 幸 and 缮. Express the contrast between the beginning and end, and polished words and appetite for gain, without an unsupported textual correction or canonical attribution.
Read 去 in context as removal of the accounts office’s control. Do not delete it or add a negation to the Chinese.
The Zhen boy is reported as thirteen; this does not establish Jia Bao-yu’s age. The boys do not meet: chapter 56 presents a dream, and chapter 57 confirms the other boy’s existence.
Retain 天风馋 and give its contextual weather sense. Do not expand the Chinese to a more familiar expression.
Retain 气血亏柔, 熔化 and 痰裹 in their historical medical setting. Do not standardize the Chinese to modern clinical terminology or add a modern diagnosis.
Read 情常 conservatively in the surrounding expression of attachment. 文具 at chapter 57 block 32 is a dressing case, not modern stationery. The Chinese remains unchanged.

Keep the relative time signals and narrative transitions around the wake, Qingming and the later paper-burning recollection. Do not import another passage’s month or silently alter a day for consistency.

sourceReadingLimits.guidance: Aunt Xue’s suggestion, the others’ approval and Nightingale’s urging do not establish that Grandmother Jia has been approached or that an engagement is settled.

Distinguish the elderly imperial consort from the senior and younger consorts of the Prince of Beijing’s household. Retain 许 rather than replacing it with Qin-shi. Preserve early breakfast and breakfast as meals.
Preserve twelve actresses, four or five departures and eight named assignments. Do not infer an exact four departures and rewrite the source.
Retain the author-selected 修树 and its pruning sense. A different external reading does not reopen the choice.
Read 我夜 as the night reference in context without adding a missing character. Read 佯常 as an unconcerned manner. Retain the source spelling 自已 rather than applying a general correction.
Retain 花掰 in chapter 58. A separate chapter 62 sound-and-meaning choice does not authorize a global spelling replacement.
Keep 绛云轩 in the chapter 59 Chinese title and use the established English place name Crimson Rue Studio. English naming continuity does not authorize changing 云 to 芸.

Distinguish Mamma He, her mother; Mamma Xia, her maternal aunt and Ou-guan’s godmother; and the unnamed paternal aunt who guards the flowers. 小女 does not make Swallow the youngest when Xiao-jiu is her younger sister.
Retain the established servant sense of 奴几, not a numerical reading. Keep 拾头打滚 and express the struggle in context without asserting an unsupported Chinese replacement.
Ai-guan does not know the true reason for the burnt paper, and Tan-chun does not certify her inference. Chan-jie’s 老娘 is her maternal grandmother, as the narration explicitly establishes.
Retain 问到蝉儿脸上. Express the direct provocation in context without replacing the Chinese verb on unsupported grounds.
Preserve the narrative return to Bao-yu’s avoidance of the quarrel. Do not rearrange the paragraphs into a falsely linear sequence.

Preserve the half-cup given, the bowl mixed with water and the remaining half-cup without inventing concentration or capacity. The preparation and benefits of fuling frost remain the aunt’s account, not scientific certification.
